example_summary: MKG Agency partnership deed requires paying 20% of profits to mother after father's death; reconstituted firm paid ₹ 1 lakh in PY 2025-26 and claimed exclusion as diversion of income by overriding title.
source_provision:
### Statutory Summary Matrix: Diversion vs Application of Income

| Doctrine / Concept | Statutory Provision | Core Legal Test / Condition | Tax Treatment & Judicial Precedent |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Diversion of Income by Overriding Title** | Section 4 | Creation of a legal charge or obligation prior to receipt where income never reaches the assessee's hands as beneficial owner | Excluded from the total income of the recipient entity; treated as income of the rightful holder (CIT vs. Nariman B. Bharucha & Sons) |
| **Application of Income** | Section 4 | Disposing of income after it has already accrued or been received by the assessee pursuant to a voluntary obligation | Included in the total income of the assessee; no deduction allowed for such application |


> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Core Statutory Test**: The fundamental distinction rests on whether the obligation diverts the source of income itself or merely applies the income after it is received.


> [!WARNING]
> **Judicial Precedent**: As established in *CIT vs. Nariman B. Bharucha & Sons (1981)*, overriding statutory or contractual charges created prior to receipt successfully divert income at source.

director.justification: The core legal issue is classifying the payment as either a 'Diversion of Income by Overriding Title' or an 'Application of Income' to determine its taxability in the hands of the firm.
director.visual_metaphor: A pipeline junction where a 'Legal Charge' valve diverts 20% of the flow into a separate tank before it reaches the main meter.
